Who runs the short stays in a place

Source: R/host_mix.R
host_mix.Rd

Splits a place's listings by how many listings their host runs across Victoria. A host with one listing is usually someone renting out their own place or holiday home. A host with ten or more is almost always a management company. The result also reports how many listings in the place are hotel rooms or serviced apartments advertised on Airbnb.

Usage

host_mix(
  places,
  baseline = "Melbourne CBD",
  active_only = TRUE,
  listings = staysvic::vic_listings
)

Arguments

places

Character vector of place names.

baseline

A place that is always included for comparison. Defaults to "Melbourne CBD". Use NULL to leave it out.

active_only

If TRUE (the default), only count listings with at least one review in the last 12 months, which filters out listings that are left up but rarely booked.

listings

Listing data. Defaults to vic_listings.

Value

A tibble with one row per place and host tier, containing place, host_tier, listings, share (proportion of the place's listings), total (all listings in the place), hotel_share (proportion that are hotel rooms or serviced apartments) and entire_share (proportion that are entire homes).

See also

top_operators() for the biggest operators in one place.

Examples

host_mix(c("Lorne", "Torquay"))
#> # A tibble: 9 × 7
#>   place         host_tier          listings share total hotel_share entire_share
#>   <chr>         <fct>                 <int> <dbl> <int>       <dbl>        <dbl>

#> 4 Lorne         Single listing           93 0.318   292     0.0274         0.962
#> 5 Lorne         2 to 9 listings          55 0.188   292     0.0274         0.962
#> 6 Lorne         10 or more listin…      144 0.493   292     0.0274         0.962
#> 7 Torquay       Single listing          265 0.447   593     0.00337        0.929
#> 8 Torquay       2 to 9 listings          91 0.153   593     0.00337        0.929
